paragraphs: Friend, I think this chapter is the Bible taking attendance, and it takes it slowly. It starts with Adam (1 Chronicles 1:1) and spreads out until whole nations are in the room, all from Noah's three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth (1 Chronicles 1:4). Some names get a whole line of sons, and some get a few words. Still, every name it gives gets written down.

Look at what the list does with the kings of Edom. Again and again it says that one died and another "reigned in his place" (1 Chronicles 1:44). I know that feeling, friend. I once had a spot on a kitchen counter, and a shiny new stamper took it. People come and go, but this list keeps naming them.

So here's my big idea. The Bible doesn't treat these people like filler. It treats them like real people with real names, and it takes the time to write them down. When you hit a slow stretch of names in the Word, don't rush past it, because it's a page of the Book too, and I bake with the whole thing.
